name: Nephrite
physical: Traditionally associated with endurance and long life
Said to bring sturdy, steady feelings
Folk tradition links it with comfort around the lower back
summary: Nephrite is the tough, silky green jade of China, New Zealand's pounamu and Siberia, a stone of endurance, protection and heart-centred grounding.
intro: Nephrite is the older, more widespread of the two jade minerals. It is a felted mass of fine amphibole fibres that interlock like felt, which gives it a remarkable toughness, actually greater than that of jadeite despite being slightly softer. Colours cover spinach green, olive, creamy white, mutton-fat white and black, all with a soft, buttery sheen. In New Zealand it is called pounamu, in China it is yu, and in Siberia it comes as dark green boulders weathered from the Sayan mountains. It takes a beautiful polish and is easy to carve, so it has served as both tool and treasure for ages.
history: Chinese craftsmen worked nephrite as early as the Neolithic period, with the Hongshan and Liangzhu cultures producing ritual discs, called bi, and tubes, called cong. Khotan in Xinjiang supplied much of the finest white nephrite for the imperial court over centuries. The Maori of New Zealand treasure pounamu as taonga, a treasure with spirit, and carve it into hei-tiki, adzes and koru pendants, often passed through generations. Native peoples of British Columbia used nephrite for tools, and the Siberian deposits are still mined. The word nephrite comes from the Greek lapis nephriticus, meaning kidney stone, reflecting an old belief about its effects on the flank.
meaning: Crystal practitioners think of nephrite as a stone of endurance, heritage and gentle protection. Its green colour is linked to the heart chakra, while its dense, earthy character connects the heart to the root. It is said to bring stability to a household, calm to a stormy relationship and a sense of belonging to those who feel adrift. In Maori tradition pounamu is believed to carry the mana of those who have worn it, which is why gifting it is meaningful. Many people use nephrite as a reminder of resilience and a calming stone to hold during stress. Physically it is traditionally associated with endurance and with comfort in the lower back, but it is a symbolic companion only and not a treatment.
howToUse: Wear a nephrite pendant close to the heart so it warms with your skin, or carry a smooth pebble as a worry stone to rub with your thumb. Place a carved piece in the eastern part of the home for family harmony. During meditation, hold a stone in the palm and breathe slowly, imagining roots growing from the heart into the ground. Use it on a desk to support patient work. If you receive a piece as a gift, keep it close; many traditions say it should not be bought for oneself.
care: Nephrite is tough and water-safe. Rinse it with lukewarm water and wipe with a soft cloth, which also removes skin oils. Avoid harsh chemicals, ultrasonic cleaners and dye-removing solvents. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or a little time buried in earth, a practice some traditions favour. Direct sunlight is generally fine. Store carved pieces wrapped in soft cloth away from harder stones, and handle often since wear gives a lovely polish.
identify: Real nephrite feels cool, smooth and dense with a soft waxy shine and a fibrous, felt-like texture under magnification. It is rarely bright emerald green; that colour usually points to jadeite or dye. Common look-alikes are serpentine, bowenite (new jade), prehnite, aventurine, glass and dyed quartzite. Serpentine is softer and can be scratched with a knife, while nephrite resists. For valuable pieces, ask for a gemological test and for provenance, especially for antique carvings.

faq.a: Yes. Jade is the name for two distinct minerals, jadeite and nephrite. Nephrite is the more widespread one, used in China, New Zealand and Canada, and is slightly tougher than jadeite.
Pounamu is the Maori name for New Zealand greenstone, a form of nephrite. It is treasured as a taonga, and carved into pendants and tools that carry personal and ancestral meaning.

faq.q: What is nephrite jade used for?
faq.a: In crystal tradition it is chosen for protection, endurance and peaceful harmony. Its green tones link it to the heart chakra, and it is worn as a lucky, grounding talisman.
